title: What If a Single Atom Hit With a Baseball's Energy?

scenes.text: What if one atom hit with the energy of a pitched baseball? One did, in 1991.
A detector in Utah, called Fly's Eye, caught a cosmic ray carrying about 300 quintillion electron volts.
That is roughly the energy of a baseball thrown at 60 miles an hour, packed into a single atomic nucleus.
It is about 40 million times the energy of the best protons our biggest accelerators can make.
Magnetic fields in our galaxy are too weak to launch it, so it likely came from another galaxy.
Scientists still don't know what threw it, so they named it the Oh-My-God particle.
